newsitem.title: UK: Wessex Water says disappointed by UK action.
newsitem.headline: Wessex Water says disappointed by UK action.

text.p: Wessex Water Plc said on Friday it was disappointed that UK regulators decided to block its bid for South West Water Plc, adding it believed a combination would have benefitted customers and investors.
Earlier, the UK Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) announced its decision not to permit proposed bids by Wessex and Severn Trent Plc for South West Water.
DTI chief Ian Lang seconded the recommendations of the Monopolies and Mergers Commission, which had said the takeovers would be against the public interest.
In response, Wessex said it remained committed to its strategic goals of deliverying quality service and enhanced shareholder value.

"Wessex believes that there was a compelling geographical and commercial rationale to the offer it proposed and that the combination of South West Water and Wessex would have created significant benefits for both customers and investors," Wessex said in a brief statement.
The DTI's move surprised the market, which had been expecting it to allow the bids as long as price cuts of around 20 percent were promised by the bidders.
Shares in South West Water plunged 128p to 577.5p by 1106 GMT, while Severn Trent gained 37p to 612.5p and Wessex added 25p to trade at 342.5p.
Wessex announced its plan to bid for its neighbouring water company on March 7, and Severn Trent tipped its hat into the ring on March 21.
Both companies declined to put a price on their offers until the DTI had decided whether the bids could go ahead.
